title: Add benchmark-lab representative workload runners, profiling baselines and reporting pipeline (v92)
author: Ava Martinez
description: This PR adds a new set of representative workload runners for the benchmark-lab, a first-pass set of profiling baselines, and an end-to-end reporting pipeline to ingest run artifacts into the benchmark dashboard. Motivation: we need consistent, reusable runners that reflect production traffic patterns (chat, completion, embeddings, and streaming) and stable profiling baselines so regression detection works across runtime changes. This change packages runners, baseline profiles, CI orchestration for nightly profiling, and a reporting pipeline that uploads metrics and artifacts to the benchmark store. Changes include: - representative workload runners (python + Go wrappers) with workload descriptors and config templates - profiling baseline artifacts for common model families (gpt-like, llama-like) and sequence-length buckets - reporting pipeline: ingestion job, artifact metadata schema, and dashboard ingestion hooks - CI wiring: nightly job for profiling baselines and a one-off job for upgrading baseline artifacts Checklist: - [x] Implement representative runners - [x] Add profiling baseline artifacts and upload scripts - [x] Add reporting pipeline ingestion job and pub/sub wiring - [x] Add unit tests for runner config parsing - [x] Add e2e smoke test for reporting pipeline - [x] Document usage in benchmark-lab/README Related: ENG-2145 (workload standardization), ENG-2210 (profiling baselines), SUP-3421 (customer-reported regression). Rollout plan: merge to main, enable nightly profiling job behind feature flag, monitor metrics for first 48 hours, and run a controlled comparison against previous baselines. No API-breaking changes are introduced.
